name: IN-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 16 points
Incumbent Stutzman holds a large fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 4%
No public polling; a Democratic-leaning national environment is the main uncertainty
model.rationale: A sixteen-point Republican district with a well-funded incumbent leaves little room for an upset, and prediction markets agree at about four percent for Democrats. The favorable national environment for Democrats is already strong enough to matter, but it would have to be historic to close a gap this wide.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending surge against Stutzman, layered on top of a strong Democratic national environment, would be the clearest sign of a tighter race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of roughly sixteen points toward the GOP, and Republican incumbent Marlin Stutzman is seeking another term. No public general-election polling is available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, candidate finances, and betting markets, all of which point strongly toward Stutzman.

Stutzman has raised about $959,000 to challenger Kelly Thompson's roughly $309,000, and outside groups have spent modestly on his behalf. Thompson's cash on hand of about $104,000 slightly exceeds Stutzman's, but a financial edge of that size is unlikely to overcome the district's lean. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a four percent chance. A favorable national environment for Democrats is the main source of residual uncertainty, but it would need to be historically large to put this seat in play.
